summary:
# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS (for later lookup; not commentary)

## BOOK 1 of 2: "The Pomp of Yesterday" by Joseph Hocking (Gutenberg #25136; Hodder & Stoughton)

**Front matter:** Title page; epigraph Kipling "Recessional" (Far famed our Navies melt away... Lest we forget). Other titles by Hocking listed (All for a Scrap of Paper, Dearer than Life, The Curtain of Fire, The Price of a Throne, The Path of Glory, Tommy, Tommy and the Maid of Athens; Facing Fearful Odds, O'er Moor and Fen, The Wilderness, Rosaleen O'Hara, The Soul of Dominic Wildthorne, Follow the Gleam, David Baring, The Trampled Cross). Epigraph quote from General Sir William Robertson, March 2, 1918 (trust "religious convictions"). Contents: 42 chapters (I Man Without a Past ... XLII An Unfinished Story).

**Foreword (March 1918):** War nearly four years; "Why is Victory delayed?" Story is romance, suggestions for nation; statements "related to him by those in a position to know." Battle of the Somme descriptions from transcripts; author revisited Front (Thiepval, Goomecourt, La Boiselle, Contalmaison). Finished story August 1917; Russia chaos foreseen.

**Narrator:** Captain Luscombe (Cornishman, a recruiting officer, later battalion officer, under-educated soldier; was at Cambridge? no — he is a Cornish captain, friend of Sir Roger Granville). Narrates in first person; the story is his account.

**Ch I (Plymouth, early spring 1915):** Narrator meets at Plymouth harbour a young-old man (28 or 48), just landed from Bombay (came from India, lost memory, found L5 notes in vest, scars from Indians, glimpses of Germany, Berlin, Leipzig, Frankfurt, Munich, Nuremburg). Narrator takes him to hotel facing The Hoe, clothes him. Name given: "Paul Edgecumbe" (from Mount Edgecumbe, and Paul the scriptural character with strange experiences). He enlists at recruiting meeting in Plymouth hall (about 2,000 people); narrator speaks; Edgecumbe volunteers ("how can a man, who is a man, do anything else?").

**Ch II:** Narrator called to Falmouth by telegram; loses track of Edgecumbe. Lunch with Colonel Gray in Exeter; Sir Roger Granville (chairman of Plymouth meeting) speculates romance. Granitelands = Granville house. Drive; Sir Roger says George St. Mabyn dines.

**Ch III:** Norah Blackwater (about 25, tall, stylish, furtive look; engaged previously to Maurice St. Mabyn, heir killed in Egypt by Arabs/rebels; now loved by George St. Mabyn). Lorna Bolivick (about 19–20, brown eyes, child-like, "ugly as sin" by her claim, father "dad" reads Blackmore; brothers; lives at Bolivick near South Petherwin, five miles away). George St. Mabyn (~28, ex-Territorial captain, wounded at Ypres, home on leave, face goes haggard at talk of Maurice). Lorna says Maurice "ought not to have stayed in Army"; George nearly broke down when addressing tenants. Lorna makes Luscombe promise to find Edgecumbe; he writes promise in diary May 29 witnessed by Lorna. Narrator suspicious of George.

**Ch IV:** Visit to St. Mabyn's house (Elizabethan, lichen walls, near Granitelands). Captain Horace Springfield (30–35, tall, dark, lean, black hair greying, deep-lined cheeks, scar on cheek below right temple, served Egypt & India; friend of Maurice; claims Maurice killed in Egypt by "mad mullah" rising; Springfield was there). Norah says Springfield looks like snakes (said by Lorna's? Norah says it to Luscombe). George and Springfield lunch at Granitelands; Norah walks with George. Narrator sent to France.

**Ch IV–V (France, 1916):** Narrator captures/raided; captured by Germans on raid, held in dug-out; Edgecumbe appears as English prisoner who persuades 30 German soldiers to surrender, leading them to British lines; Sergeant Smith with narrator. Edgecumbe in British uniform (D.C.L.I.).

**Ch VI–VII:** Edgecumbe's memory; narrator's suspicion Edgecumbe = Maurice (dismissed by Lorna's letter/photo later). Colonel reports Edgecumbe missing; Edgecumbe returns wounded (drugged Germans, shell hole). Edgecumbe's temperance/"drink" speech: Government allowed drink, firemen drunk, munitions wasted. George St. Mabyn arrives as Major, nervous at Edgecumbe.

**Ch VIII:** Narrator eavesdrops at copse near St. Pinto: George and Springfield plot; Springfield: "if it is he, he must never go back to England alive"; George engaged to Norah. Note from George.

**Ch IX–X:** Edgecumbe missing after leaving narrator's billet (pistol shot near St. Pierre). Lorna's letter (wants photo; hospital; patient with no legs). Battle of the Somme 1 July; narrator captured by Germans, then Edgecumbe rescues him (three Germans); Edgecumbe says "I have found more than life." Edgecumbe reports converted: Y.M.C.A. hut, New Testament, God, Christ.

**Ch XI–XIV:** Edgecumbe's story: quarry, old man rescued him; Y.M.C.A.; conversion. Edgecumbe hears Springfield's Indian cry; "I know that voice!" Lorna's letter praising Edgecumbe's face. Edgecumbe's logic: drink, Christianity, war must be fought in God's strength; quotes Sir William Robertson, Admiral Beatty ("Make the men religious, Bishop"; "When England looks out with humbler eyes..."); Lloyd George quote; Victor Hugo "Napoleon lost Waterloo because God was against him." Colonel Heywood (OTC CO) says Edgecumbe is an artillery officer. Lorna's letter invites them to Bolivick.

**Ch XV–XVII:** Devonshire arrival at Bolivick; Sir Thomas Bolivick (baronet). Charlie Buller (24, first lieutenant Devonshire yeomanry, suitor of Lorna). Springfield and Buller arrive. Edgecumbe falls in love with Lorna at sight ("The Gates of heaven"). Springfield saved (Edgecumbe dug him out) - Springfield thanks Edgecumbe.

**Ch XVIII–XIX:** Edgecumbe poisoned mysteriously (suspicion Springfield); Dr. Merril (South Petherwin); Colonel McClure (St George's Military Hospital, Plymouth, 12 years India) fetched by narrator driving Buller's car ~50 miles; Springfield left; McClure detects blue spot on Edgecumbe's left arm (Indian poison).

**Ch XX–XXII:** McClure saves Edgecumbe (injects antidote). Edgecumbe declares love; narrator warns of wife possibility. Springfield visits Lorna; Springfield's peerage claim (heir to Lord Carbis, brewer, created 1890).

**Ch XXIII–XXIV:** Springfield-Narrator conversation; Edgecumbe's proposal to Lorna in woods (October autumn); Lorna refuses; Sir Thomas admires Edgecumbe.

**Ch XXV–XXVII:** London trip; Edgecumbe, House of Commons, Cabinet Minister; Waterloo station; music-hall; "Where does God come in?"; Edgecumbe's arguments on Christianity, drink.

**Ch XXVIII–XXIX:** London sights, Springfield's engagement to Lorna; Springfield's threats; Edgecumbe on drink, food famine; Springfield gazetted colonel.

**Ch XXX–XXXI (1917):** Edgecumbe's letters: Vimy, Lens, Russia revolution, Wilson/America; Edgecumbe returns wounded, D.S.O.; Springfield tried to discredit him (accused of German uniform); Times article.

**Ch XXXII–XXXIII:** Edgecumbe's speech at public meeting (London, drink & impurity); General: "worth more than an army corps." Carbis parents arrive; Edgecumbe = Jack Carbis, son of Lord Carbis (brewer); mother: "John! Jack!" Edgecumbe's memory returns.

**Ch XXXIV–XXXVI:** Memory; Lady Carbis; doctor Merril; Jack Carbis's intention to refuse father's drink-money; Lorna says Springfield.

**Ch XXXVII–XXXIX:** Jack tells narrator of Maurice St. Mabyn (alive in July 1914; saw him in Bizna; Springfield tried to murder him; Gregory; Maurice imprisoned by Turks, released after Baghdad). Jack exposes Springfield at Bolivick dinner; Maurice St. Mabyn appears alive; Springfield withdraws.

**Ch XL–XLII:** Maurice's generosity; Springfield found dead (poison injected; suicide letter "Life's not worth living..."). Narrator visits Bolivick; Lorna explains Springfield's threat (blackmail about Jack's Indian past). Jack and Lorna engaged (narrator blesses; Jack goes "to beard the lion" with Sir Thomas). End.

---

## BOOK 2 of 2: "For God and Gold" by Julian Corbett (Gutenberg #62184; Macmillan 1900; first ed. 1887)

**Front matter:** Title; dedication "Calling on this ailing age... Mr. Jasper Festing, sometime Fellow of Trinity College, Cambridge, late officer in Her Majesty's Sea-Service... Voyage to Nombre de Dios under Sir Francis Drake, Knight, written by himself." Preface by J.C. (Thames Ditton, Oct 1887) explains "Sir Francis Drake Revived" (1626), Preacher Philip Nichols, Pike/Culverin word-play, Signor Giampietro Pugliano, Sir Philip Sidney letter; Antwerp caravel. "Mr. Waldyve" also named.

**Narrator:** Jasper Festing, first person, memoir written in later age.

**Ch I (c. 1558–59; father Nicholas Festing dies January, first year of Elizabeth's reign, at Longdene near Medway, Upchurch marshes; Puritan; ex-wool merchant, former Frankfurt exile). Cicely (nurse, married to steward Miles). Father's words: "God-a-mercy on usurers." Longdene = former Austin Canons house. Harry Waldyve (son of Sir Fulke Waldyve of Ashtead, old knight, friend of Festing; Harry's mother died in childbed; Harry personated Princess Cleopatra in masque). Sir Fulke swears roundly.

**Ch II:** Funeral: Mr. Drake (Master Drake, Chatham, preacher to fleet, red-faced, blue merry eyes, tarry hand) and Mr. Death (sour, pale). Drake reads will: body buried by reformed rites, no bells, no incense. Funeral at Upchurch-area church (Longdene church, ruined rood-screen, pigeons, jackdaws), Mr. Drake's sermon, singing Paternoster; Festing weeps.

**Ch III:** Festing and Sir Fulke; Rochester; Mr. Drake on capstan similitude; Drake's house = old hulk on Medway ("no man's land," ship said to be Cabot's); Drake fled Tavistock (Six Articles). Drake's boys: John (eldest), Joseph (Joe), James (apprenticed to Spain, lost), Jack, Francis/"Frank" (eldest brother, mariner, away), Willie (baby with sword-hilt), Edward? Mrs. Drake (thin, weary, sorrowful). Boys fight; Jack vs Festing. Harry and Festing with Drake sons; Frank's talk. Tutor Mr. Follet (Christopher Follet, Aristotle, "Ramus Ransacked"). Festing reads cosmography, Earthly Paradise.

**Ch IV:** Sir Fulke trains boys; Harry to Lord Russell (Earl of Bedford) household. Festing to Trinity College Cambridge with Follet; Drake with them to Gravesend/London. Dr. Beaumont (Master of Trinity); Mr. Thomas Cartwright (major-fellow, Puritan); Festing's riot at effigy ("Fasting Johnnie" at Saunderson). Vice-Master John Beaumont arrested by Proctor after Saunderson suit; Sir William Cecil (Secretary).

**Ch V:** Summer 1564; Queen Elizabeth's progress to Cambridge; Festing: "Vivat Regina Divina." Cartwright's disputation; Lord Robert Dudley visits Cartwright at night; Festing warned; Queen's Dido play; Queen leaves Aug 10.

**Ch VI:** Festing returns to Ashtead; Harry married (Nan = Anne St John, ruddy hair, brown eyes, Bedford's niece). Harry's Berwick service under Earl; Frank Drake returns from Indies. Harry, Festing, Frank sail on Gazehound fishing; they take Antwerp caravel (Spanish, arrows). Festing hear pirate talk; Frank (captain, Spanish-treachery story of James Drake). Festing's guilt.

**Ch VII:** Capture of caravel; Festing kills cavalier (Spanish gentleman) with rapier; Queen's ship Minion (Captain David Carlet) passes; Mrs. Drake pleads; Festing returns to Ashtead; Sir Fulke's men & cargo hidden.

**Ch VIII:** Festing reproves Frank re piracy; accepts; Frank's license argument; Harry leaves for Italy; Cambridge Puritans; Festing elected fellow; Whitgift succeeds Beaumont 1567; Festing resigns fellowship.

**Ch IX:** Sir Fulke dies (Catholic priest "Mr. Carter"); Frank's Hawkins voyage (San Juan de Ulloa). Frank and Festing: Culverin (Sergeant Alexander Culverin; "Signor John Peter Pugliano, esquire"); Harry returns; Frank's plan.

**Ch X–XI:** Harry married Nan; Festing lonely; Harry's Italianate atheism; Nan's Puritan turn; Festing's seduction-sin with Nan; sermon at Upchurch (Mr. Drake vs Mr. Death; Drake's text John x.13 "The hireling fleeth"). Communion. Festing courts Nan; Harry's speech on nature.

**Ch XII:** 1572 Frank plans Nombre de Dios. Nan's despair; she begs Festing to take her away; Festing kisses her.

**Ch XIII–XIV:** Flight to inn at night; Harry arrives; flings rapier through window; Festing's oath on Harry's rapier; Nan's letter "To Mrs. Waldyve" from Harry; Harry gone to Rochester/London; Festing to London, Mr. Follet's advice (divining rod, Pythagorean music).

**Ch XV:** Festing meets Frank and John Oxenham at St Paul's; ruffian bully; Oxenham's romantic talk of West Indies.

**Ch XVI–XVII:** Festing merchant of expedition; Plymouth; Whitsunday; sails 23 May 1572?; confrontation with Harry in Frank's cabin; reconciliation at sea; Sergeant's comment; voyage to Guadeloupe, Dominica; Port Pheasant; Spanish intelligence; fort; Ranse on Lion; articles signed 13 July 1572.

**Ch XVIII:** Nombre de Dios attack (night, bell ringing, Plaza, silver bars, rain storm, Drake wounded in leg; Culverin's silk scarf binds leg); Bastimentos island; Spanish envoy ("Captain Drake" sought); Diego; Frank burns Swan (Tom Moone's spike-gimlet). Cimaroons, chief Pedro, Port Plenty.

**Ch XIX–XX:** Spanish captives; Pedro; fort Diego; Cimaroon alliance; Jack Drake's death at frigate attack (Allen dies; Jack disobeys Frank's orders; psalm; "Frank always knew best").

**Ch XXI:** Mosquitoes; Frank's calenture; Joe Drake dies; Frank dissects corpse (surgeon, Vicary's Anglishman's Treasure); Spanish Señorita (black-eyed, Treasurer of Lima's daughter? at this point "Scrivano of Tolu's daughter") attacks Frank; Festing guards her; Cimaroons attack at night; Señorita kisses Festing ("Gasparo"). Festing's love affair with Señorita.

**Ch XXII–XXIII:** Crossing isthmus; view of South Sea; Panama; Culverin's drunkenness; ambush of recua; Treasurer's gold lost; Venta Cruz; Culverin punished (hobby-horse).

**Ch XXIV–XXVI:** Veragua plan; Frenchman Captain Tetú (70 Huguenots) and St. Bartholomew news; Señorita's talk ("Gasparo"); recua on Chagres; silver captured (~25 tons); Tetú captured; raft through surf; Harry gives up place to Festing.

**Ch XXVII–XXVIII:** Festing and Oxenham rivalry; Festing duels Oxenham (Italian fence); Señorita confesses forced marriage to old husband (Lima); "Gasparo," kiss. Oxenham later hanged at Lima. Ship Pasha; return via Havana; arrival Plymouth 9 Aug 1573; Festing & Harry ride to Ashtead; Nan reconciled; Culverin keeps stable. Ending: "THE END".

---

Key names: Nicholas Festing (father), Cicely, Miles, Lashmer (Miles's son, servant), Sir Fulke Waldyve, Harry (Henry) Waldyve, Nan (Anne St. John, Mrs. Waldyve), little Fulke (son), Mr. Drake (Ned, father), Mrs. Drake, Frank Drake, John (Jack) Drake, Joe, James, Willie, Mr. Follet, Mr. Cartwright, Dr. Beaumont, Culverin, Oxenham, Diego, Pedro, Tetú, Mr. Death, Carlet (Minion), Ranse (Lion), Overy, Tom Moone, Allen, Robert, Señorita (Gasparo nickname), Earl of Bedford, Dr. Whitgift, Bruno (later friend).
